name: BH1750 ambient light sensor
description: ROHM digital ambient light sensor measuring 1 to 65535 lx (1 lx resolution in H-resolution mode) with an I2C interface; the chip runs on 2.4-3.6 V. Sold as: GY-302 BH1750 module (5-pin: VCC, GND, SCL, SDA, ADDR) with an on-board 3.3 V regulator and 4.7 k pull-ups, powered from 3-5 V, I2C address 0x23 (0x5C with ADDR high).
eli5: Tells your board how bright the light around it is, in lux, like a camera's light meter.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Module supply, 3-5 V (an on-board 3.3 V regulator feeds the chip)

pins.description: I2C clock (4.7 k pull-up to the module's 3.3 V on board)

pins.description: I2C data (4.7 k pull-up to the module's 3.3 V on board)

pins.name: ADDR
pins.description: Address select, 4.7 k pull-down on board: unconnected/low = 0x23, high (3.3 V, not 5 V) = 0x5C

supplierQuery: GY-302 BH1750 light sensor module I2C
buildNotes: Send one opcode per I2C write (the chip needs a STOP after each): Power On 0x01, then One-Time H-Resolution 0x20, wait up to 180 ms, then read 2 bytes MSB first.
Illuminance in lux = raw / 1.2 with the default measurement-time register (MTreg = 69); the H-resolution range tops out at 54612 lx.
Leave ADDR unconnected (4.7 k pull-down on the GY-302) for address 0x23. For 0x5C tie ADDR to 3.3 V only: it goes straight to the chip, whose absolute maximum is 4.5 V, so never tie it to 5 V.
Keep the sensor window uncovered and facing the light; the board's own LEDs or a shadow from wires will change the reading.

driver.code:
# BH1750 ambient light sensor (ROHM BH1750FVI), MicroPython driver.
# One-time H-resolution mode (opcode 0x20): 1 lx resolution, 120 ms typ / 180 ms max,
# then the chip returns to power-down by itself. lux = raw / 1.2 (default MTreg = 69).
# The chip accepts one opcode per I2C transaction (a STOP after every opcode).
import time

POWER_DOWN = 0x00
POWER_ON = 0x01
RESET = 0x07
ONE_TIME_H_RES = 0x20


class BH1750:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x23):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr  # 0x23 with ADDR low (default on GY-302), 0x5C with ADDR high
        self._cmd(POWER_ON)
        self._cmd(RESET)  # clears the data register; only works in power-on mode
        self._cmd(POWER_DOWN)

    def _cmd(self, op):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([op]))

    def lux(self):
        """Measure once and return the illuminance in lux."""
        self._cmd(POWER_ON)
        self._cmd(ONE_TIME_H_RES)
        time.sleep_ms(180)  # max H-resolution measurement time
        d = self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, 2)
        raw = (d[0] << 8) | d[1]
        return raw / 1.2

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from bh1750 import BH1750

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = BH1750(i2c)
while True:
    print('Light: %.1f lx' % sensor.lux())
    time.sleep(1)
